The engine's four entry points: $0200 loads the stage named by $D0 and enters it (the loader's boot jumps here with $D0 = 0, and stages jump here to load the next), $0203 shows THE END and waits for a key, $0206 restarts the demo (CONTROL-R), $0209 starts a game (the title stage, on a key).
THE END: stages jump here when the hero has died (or the demo is over); runs to $025E.
Restart the demo: CONTROL-R in play jumps here ($772F) with A = the stage number.
Start a game: the title stage jumps here when a key is pressed at the title ($B7E7); runs to $0237.

Load stage $D0 with the loader ($0300) until it reads without error and the stage's last three bytes check: $BFFD must equal $D0, $BFFE $D0 EOR $3B and $BFFF $D0 EOR $49; it retries the whole load until they do. Then copies $D0 into $D2, sets the draw page ($07) to $40 and enters the stage through its vector at $BFFA.
Enter the loaded stage: $D2 = $D0, draw on page 2 ($07 = $40), and jump to the stage's entry, $BFFA.

Start a game: clear the draw page ($1900) and, unless page 1 was the one drawn on, flip ($7609) and clear the other too, then flip; then show the castle picture ($0303), play the tune the title stage keeps at $1012, set $D0 = 1 (the cliff) and $DC = 0, and load the cliff ($020C).
Show the page just cleared ($7609).
Count $D2 down once and show the castle picture ($0303 returns A = 0, so the BNE back never branches); then the tune, $D0 = 1, $DC = 0, and load the cliff.

THE END: draw the words ($02CB), then poll about 65,000 times for a key ($C000), or for either joystick button ($C061, $C062) when $C4 says joystick, and start a game on one ($02B4). If none comes, flip ($7609) and go back to the title: re-enter the title stage ($022C) if it is the one loaded ($D2 = 0), otherwise set $D0 = 0 and load it ($020C).
No key in time: flip pages, then back into the title stage if $D2 is 0, else reload the title stage.
CONTROL-R's restart (through $0206): clear both pages and continue as if no key came ($0291), which returns to the title and its demo.
A key or button at THE END: flip pages and set $DC = 1; if the cliff is the stage loaded ($D2 = 1), enter it again as it is ($022C), otherwise set $D0 = 1 and load it ($020C).
Clear the draw page, draw THE END on it ($02E7) and show it ($7609), then clear the other page; when that is page 2, draw the words there too, flip again and clear.
Draw THE END, the shape at $9A74 (10 rows of 10 bytes), at byte column 15, row 90, stored over what is there ($0F = 1), through the stage's shape routine at $1903.
Two bytes after THE END's routine, $19 $DF; nothing reads them.
The loader's two entry points: $0300 loads what A names (a stage's number, $10 for the castle picture), $0303 loads and shows the castle picture.
JMP: load the castle picture and show it ($03A5).

The disk controller's slot times 16, $60 for slot 6, which the loader reads into X for every access to the drive ($C08C,X and the rest); $0307-$0308 hold $C600, the address of slot 6's boot ROM, through which the reset handler boots the disk again ($0335).

The reset handler (page 3's soft-reset vector $03F2, and the language card's copy of the ROM's reset vector at $FFFC): loads 'R' and skips the next load with BIT; the BRK handler at $030C loads 'P'. Either way it initialises the text screen (INIT, HOME), puts the letter at the top left of text page 1, clears $0800-$BFFF a page at a time while clicking the speaker, copies the ROM into the language card again ($03DC), spoils the power-up byte ($03F4) and jumps to the boot ROM at $C600 ($0307): reset or a BRK reboots the disk.
The BRK handler (page 3's vector $03F0): the same as reset with 'P' on the screen.
The page of the STA above, counted up from $08 by the INC at $0325 until it reaches $C0: the page being cleared.

Load from the disk: A says what. Swaps zero page with $4F00 ($0393), turns the drive's motor on and reads two pages from the track under the head into $4000 (each sector found by the marks F5 D5 DA, each byte made of two disk bytes, a ROL and an AND, closing with the mark FB), then calls the second stage of the loader at $4000 with A, swaps zero page back and returns A = 0. A read that fails its closing mark starts the two pages again.

ASL $FFFF, once per page read: it changes no memory, since the language card is not write-enabled while the game runs (orientation.md, "Steady state"), and spends six cycles between the page's last byte and the test for the closing mark.
Swap zero page with $4F00-$4FFF, so that the loader's own variables are kept apart from the game's; returns A = 0.

Load the castle picture (A = $10) into $A000-$BFFF, draw on page 2, clear it ($1900), show page 2, copy the 32 pages from $A000 to $2000 (page 1) with $03C3, then show page 1: the castle picture before the cliff.
Copy X pages of 256 bytes from the page in A to the page in Y.

Copy the ROM into the language card: two reads of $C081 write-enable the card's RAM with the ROM still read, then the 48 pages from $D000 are copied onto themselves, which writes the ROM's bytes into the RAM beneath, and $C082 leaves the ROM switched in and the card protected. Called by the reset handler.

Page 3's vectors as the game sets them: $03EE-$03EF unused (0, 0); $03F0-$03F1 the BRK vector, $030C; $03F2-$03F3 the soft-reset vector, $0309; $03F4 the power-up byte, $A6 ($03 EOR $A5), which makes the ROM take a reset as warm and go through $03F2.
Turn the drive's motor on ($C089,X) and wait twice through the Monitor's WAIT with A = 0, the longest it waits, for the motor to come up to speed.

The text routine's glyphs ($0700): 30 shapes in the shape routine's format (height, width in bytes, then the rows), for the character codes $61-$7E of the game's own alphabet (facts.md, "The text alphabet"); $60 is a space and has none. Character n's glyph is at $0680+n (low byte) and $06A0+n plus 4 (high). The first, 'a', is 10 rows of 2 bytes.
The low bytes of the glyphs' addresses, one per character code minus $60 (the text routine at $0700 subtracts $60 from each character); code 0 draws nothing.
The high bytes of the glyphs' addresses less 4: the text routine adds 4, so 0, 1 and 2 are pages $04, $05 and $06.
Each character's advance in whole bytes of 7 dots, added to the column after it is drawn.
Each character's advance in extra dots (0-6), added to the dot position; at 7 or more the routine carries a byte into the column.

Draw one line of the game's own alphabet. ($E5) points at the line: a byte column, a dot offset (0-6), then character codes, $60 a space and $61-$7E the glyphs at $0400, ended by any byte below $60. Each glyph is drawn through the shape routine at $1903 at the row in $06, ORed on the draw page ($0F = 0), and the position moves on by the character's width ($06C0 bytes, $06E0 dots). A glyph that would reach below row $C0 has the height in its header cut for the draw and put back after it. Called by the title stage for the prologue and by the last stage for the closing text.
A shape of 9 rows of 3 bytes, after the text routine; nothing in the engine or any stage points at it.
Two entry points for the title stage: $0780 copies the shown page two rows up onto the draw page, the prologue's scroll; $0783 flips pages and remembers the page now shown.

Copy the screen up two rows: each of the 190 rows from the top takes the 40 bytes of the row two below it on page $E4 (the one shown), written to the draw page ($07). $07B9 sets up the two row pointers. The title stage calls it once for each step of the prologue's scroll.

The title stage's page flip: show the page just drawn on ($C054 or $C055, after the IIe's wait for the vertical blank, $07D7), make the other the draw page, and keep the shown page's number in $E4 for the scroll copy. It does not clear the right edge, as the game's own flip ($7609) does.
Row pointers for the scroll: $E0/$E1 = row X on the draw page, $E2/$E3 = row X+2 on page $E4; returns with X one more than it came.
Wait for the vertical blank on a IIe or IIc: when the ROM's ID byte $FBB3 is 6, loop while $C019's bit 7 says the beam is not in the blank. On an older machine it returns at once.

Bytes nothing reads, after the scroll routines: the last eight, $07F8-$07FF, are the same as the last eight of the title stage's load at $BFF8-$BFFF (its entry, JMP $B760, and its check bytes 00 3B 49), left there when the disk was made.

Play the tune at ($F7) on the speaker in two voices. The header's first byte is the tempo (written into the count at $0D5D) and its second the page of the second voice's click (written into the LDA at $0D86: $C0 clicks the speaker). Then notes of three bytes: the length, and the pitch as a coarse and a fine count; both voices count the same pitch, the second one count shorter, so that they beat; a coarse count with bit 7 set is a rest. $FD n writes LDY #n at $0D79, which resets the second voice's count to n at each click of the first; $FE writes two NOPs there instead; $FF ends the tune. Before each note a key that is down goes to the special keys ($7603) and is cleared, so it never reaches the game; if the music or the sound is now off ($4F AND $86 zero) the tune ends.
The tempo: the LDA's operand, written from the tune's first byte ($0D04), the count put in $FE for each pass of a note's middle loop.
The first byte of the pair the tune's $FD and $FE commands rewrite: LDY (for $FD n) or NOP (for $FE).
The second byte at $0D79: a NOP, or the count of LDY #n after $FD n ($0D44).
The page of the second voice's LDA, written from the tune's second byte ($0D0A): $C0 clicks the speaker, another page reads without a sound.
Zeros between the tune player and the sampled sound.

Play the recorded sound: the 256 bytes at $0E00-$0EFF, eight one-bit samples a byte, top bit first. For each sample it waits $BA times round a loop and clicks the speaker only when the sample differs from the one before, so that the cone follows the samples. $9C-$9F hold the pointer and the end. The frame routine plays it when $4E counts down to zero: set when an opponent falls dead ($BA = $1E), when the hero does against the opponent of type 1 ($BA = $28, slower and lower), and when a doorway is kicked open ($BA = $1E).
The sampled sound's pointers: $0DFB-$0DFD are copied into $9D-$9F (start page $0E, end $0EFF); $0DFA and $0DFE-$0DFF are not read.
The recorded sound, 2,048 one-bit samples played by $0DC0, top bit first, at two speeds.

Sixteen bytes where a cutscene keeps the opponent's record ($70-$7F) while it uses the record for a guard walking in ($7A57, $7A62). As loaded, they and the bytes to $0FAF read as tunes of two bytes a note, a length and a pitch, with $FF after each tune: a form the tune player at $0D00 does not take, and nothing points at them.
The last stage's death tune ($1003 there), for the play routine ($0D00): tempo 6, the second voice on the speaker; a rest, then a short phrase.
The four notes the last stage plays the first time the hero takes the stance in room 5 ($100F there): tempo 7, the second voice on the speaker.

The loader's second stage, read from the track the head is parked on (track 1) by $0338, which calls it with A holding what to load. It reads the third stage into $5000-$57FF: four sectors of two pages each, from half tracks 4, 5, 4 and 5 (tracks 2 and 2.5, stepping back and forth between them, $4148), then jumps to $5000 with A.
Read four sectors of two pages each into the pages from A on, stepping the head by $4148 after each.
The first page of each run of four sectors to read, $50, ended by 0.

Read one sector of two pages into page A. Each sector has its own mark: $414C's byte for the sector number ($04), then the number shifted right OR $AA, then the number OR $AA; after each page of data, $F5 ($4154). Each byte of data is two disk bytes, the first rotated left and ANDed with the second. A sector with a wrong end mark is read again from its start.
The page count, 2, is written into the LDX at $4069.
The LDX's operand, the number of pages in a sector, written by $4066; from here the sector's marks are looked for.
ASL $FFFF: an instruction that changes nothing, for its time between two disk bytes.
Move the head to half track A, with longer steps (X = $13 into $4123).
BIT $0AA2 here hides LDX #$0A, the first instruction of seek ($40BD), from a caller entering at $40BA, which keeps X = $13; the BIT only sets flags.

Move the head to half track A from $1F, one half track at a time through the four phase magnets ($C080-$C087 of the slot in $0306), each step's wait from $412D (magnet on) and $4139 (magnet off), shorter as the move goes on.
Switch the phase magnet for half track $1F on (carry set) or off (carry clear).
Switch the phase magnet for half track A on (carry set) or off: A AND 3, doubled, plus the carry, plus the slot ($0306), indexes $C080-$C087.
Wait A times $4123's count (the LDX's operand, set by $40BA and $40BD).
The wait's count, the LDX's operand: $13 from $40BA, $0A from $40BD.
The wait after each step's magnet is switched on, by the step's number (0-11), the first steps longest.
The wait after the magnet is switched off, by the step's number.
The half track the head is moving to.
The number of steps taken so far in this move.
The half track the head was on before the step.
The head's move after each of the four sectors, in half tracks: +1, -1, +1, +1.
The first byte of each sector's mark, by the sector number's low three bits.
The sector's end mark, $F5, then zeros to the end of the page.

The loader's third stage, from $4000 with A holding what to load: negative is the boot ($5300); $10 the castle picture, from half track 8 (track 4) through row $00 of $5400; a stage number n, from half track 8n + $0E (track 4n + 7) through row $30. After the read, the game's zero page comes back from $4F00, and the bytes $78-$7F and $F8-$FF of every page of $4000-$5FFF are cleared: the parts of the second hi-res page that are never shown.
A zero between the routines.
The castle picture: from half track 8 (track 4), through row $00 of $5400.
Five NOPs where something was taken out.
Two PLAs drop the return into $0338 (after its JSR $4000), so that the RTS at $504D returns straight to $0338's caller, with A = 0; the copy back from $4F00 takes the place of $0338's swap.
Zeros, then from $5100 bytes left in memory when the disk was made: code that calls ROM routines ($F12C, $FEFD, $FF3A and others). Nothing runs it.

The boot's last step: reset the stack, read the engine (row $70 of $5400, from half track $36, track 27), clear zero page, turn the music and sound on ($4F, $86), set the stage to 0 ($D0) and $D2 to $FF, and start the game at $0200.
Zeros to the end of the page.

For each load, the page each sector of each track goes to, twelve to a track, ended by 0. Row $00, the castle picture: $A0-$BF, then four sectors all into page $40, each over the last: 36 sectors. Row $30, a stage: $10-$1F and $A0-$BF, 48 sectors. Row $70, the engine: $08-$0F and $60-$9F, 72 sectors.
Zeros after the last row, to the end of the page.

Read whole tracks from half track A, two half tracks (one track) apart, each into the twelve pages its row of $5400 gives (Y), until the next entry is 0; then the head goes back to half track 2 (track 1, where the second stage is) and the motor is turned off ($C088).
A BRK after a branch that is always taken.
PLA and RTS that nothing reaches.
Take this track's four marks from $5610 by the half track ($1F / 2): three bytes before the track's data and one after each sector; then read it ($570F).
Zeros between the routines.
The end of a load: back to half track 2, the motor off, and return.
More bytes left in memory when the disk was made, code that calls ROM routines; nothing runs it. Then 16 bytes at $5600 that no disk byte can index ($5600 + Y is read only with Y = $80-$FF).
16 bytes that no disk byte can index: the table is read at $5600 + Y only with Y = $80-$FF.
The marks of the tracks: four bytes from the entry the half track picks, so that each track's marks differ from the next one's.
Zeros, and the decoding table's entries for the disk bytes, $5680-$56FF: the four bits each disk byte stands for ($5747, $5753).
JMP to the seek at $576F.
The twelve pages the sectors of the track being read go to, copied from $5400 ($550D). As loaded, the last track of the engine's load, $94-$9F.

Read a track's twelve sectors: find the three marks ($A0-$A2) once, then for each sector 256 bytes, each from two disk bytes through the table at $5600 (four bits each), into the page $5703 names for it (written into the STA at $5756), and the end mark ($A3). A wrong end mark starts the whole track again.
The STA's low byte, which counts the sector's 256 bytes ($5759).
The STA's page, set from $5703 for each sector ($573D); its low byte, $5757, counts the sector's 256 bytes.
Move the head to half track A, as $40BD does, with the waits at $57D7 and $57E3.
Switch the phase magnet for half track $1F on (carry set) or off.
Switch the phase magnet for half track A on (carry set) or off, as $4114 does.
Wait A times $13 rounds.
The wait after each step's magnet is switched on, by the step's number.
The wait after it is switched off; then zeros.
The low bytes of the 42 legs shapes, one per legs pose ($20): standing, the stance, kicks, steps, the run, the bow, falling and lying dead. The shapes are at $8000-$9DFF; drawn by $6959.
The high bytes of the 42 legs shapes.
For each legs pose, the legs shape's byte column from the figure's position ($22): added facing right, taken away facing left. Signed.
For each legs pose, the legs shape's top row less 114 ($693F adds $72).

The low bytes of 42 masks, one per legs pose, shapes of rows of mostly set dots with the feet left clear. $6786 and $6789 draw one with AND ($0F = $FF) under a fighter's feet before he is drawn, so the floor's pattern does not show through his feet.
The high bytes of the 42 feet masks ($90-$95).
Each feet mask's byte column from the legs shape's (signed).
Each feet mask's top row less 114.
For each legs pose, the byte column of the torso from the figure's position: where the hips are.
For each legs pose, the dots (0-6) added to the figure's dot offset ($50) for the torso; a carry past 6 moves it a byte.

For each torso pose ($21), the head: 0-6 is the dots the head is moved forward from the torso's column, with the ordinary head; 7 and 8 select the head's second and third drawings (a head turned or bowed), with no move.
The hero's head, three drawings by head type: high bytes, $8E.
The hero's head, three drawings: low bytes ($8E9B, $8EA5, $8EB3).
The headgear of opponent type 0 ($3E), three drawings by head type: high bytes.
The headgear of type 0: low bytes ($8ECB, $8EEB, $8F0E).
The mask cut under the head before it is drawn, high byte ($8E); only the ordinary head has one, so the table's other two entries are the zeros that start $61DA and the head routine skips them.
The head mask's low byte: $8EC1.
For each torso pose, the head's byte column from the torso's (signed).
For each torso pose, the head's top row less 114.
The low bytes of the 38 torso shapes, one per torso pose ($21): the arms in the stance, punches high, middle and low, the kick's lean, blocks, the bow, falling.
The high bytes of the 38 torso shapes.
For each torso pose, the torso shape's byte column from the torso's position (signed).
For each torso pose, the torso shape's top row less 114.
For each legs pose, $FF when its shape is drawn mirrored: poses $1C-$20, the second half of the long step forward (sequence $2B-$34), which reuse the shapes of poses $1B-$17 facing the other way.
Headgear type 1's three drawings: high bytes, in the stage's memory ($BE).
Headgear type 1: low bytes ($BE00, $BE20, $BE43). The headgear of types 1-5 is each stage's own, at $BE00-$BFFF.
Headgear type 2: high bytes.
Headgear type 2: low bytes ($BE60, $BE80, $BEA3).
Headgear type 3: high bytes.
Headgear type 3: low bytes ($BEC0, $BEE0, $BF03).
Headgear type 4: high bytes.
Headgear type 4: low bytes ($BF20, $BF40, $BF63).

The legs' animation sequences: legs poses one per frame, each sequence ended by $FF. $25 is the position and $27 the step (+1, -1 to run a sequence backwards, 0 to hold); $6400 reads it. $80-$83 are commands: $80 the kick, at the height in $2A; $81 the kick's end, which goes on by the stick ($64AC); $82 the step back; $83 back to position 0. $EE holds the pose.
For each entry of the legs sequences, how far the figure moves on that frame, in byte columns, forward in the direction it faces ($2C); taken away when the sequence runs backwards.

The torso's animation sequences, read the same way through $26 and $28: torso poses, $FF to end, $84 a punch from the stance and $86 a quick punch, each at the height in $2A; other values with bit 7 set ($DD, $EE) leave the torso as it is.
Six zeros after the torso sequences.

Move the working figure ($20-$2F) on by one frame. If $27 is not 0, step the legs sequence ($6300) by it, move the figure ($22) by the step table ($6360), negated for a backward step and for facing left ($2C), and take the new legs pose into $20; $FF stops the sequence, and $80-$83 run the commands below. Then the same for the torso sequence ($63BE) through $26, $28 and $21. $2B, the blow being thrown, is set to $FF first and to the blow's type by a kick or punch command.
Sequence command $80, a kick: both halves take the kick's pose, 2, 3 or 4 for a high, middle or low kick by $2A (up, centre, down), and $2B the blow's type, 0-2; counts $45 for the swing's sound.

Sequence command $81, the kick's end: with the stick centred, or pushed forward when the opponent is less than 8 columns away ($33), back into the stance by the step sequence run backwards from $3A (the two columns it will take back added first); pushed forward further off, on into a step forward ($39); pulled back, a step back (from 5).
Sequence command $82: run the legs from $30 backwards and the torso from $39: the step back.
Torso command $86, the quick punch: torso pose $19, $1A or $1B by $2A, the blow's type 6, 7 or 8; counts $45.
Sequence command $83: both sequences back to position 0.
Torso command $84, the punch from the stance: torso pose $16, $17 or $18 by $2A, the blow's type 3, 4 or 5; counts $45.
Four bytes between the routines ($80 $D5 $FF $BF); nothing reads them.

Carry out a command for the working figure ($20-$2F). A is the command: 0 nothing but the movement by the stick ($29), $9B take the stance or stand up, $C5 a kick, $D7 a punch, $C2 a bow, $D1 change the arms ($65F4), $C6 fall dead; the height is in $2A. Standing ($2F not zero), $C2 is taken; in the stance, $D1, $D7 and $C5; $C6, $9B and the movement in either. The player's input ($6E00) and the opponents' brain ($6B00) both end here, and the stages send commands of their own.

The movement by the stick ($29, forward is the way the figure faces). Standing still (legs 7), forward starts the run (legs sequence $3F, torso $2A); running, the cycle repeats ($49 back to $41) while the stick stays forward, and stops ($49) at legs pose $23 when it does not. In the stance (legs 6), forward runs the step sequence from $37 and back runs it backwards from $3D; during a step the stick can turn it round ($27), and positions $39 and $3B lead into the longer steps at $2C and $33.
Command $D1: change the arms from the stance's (torso 6) to torso pose $1C when $2A is up, or $1D otherwise, or from one of those two to the other; then the movement. The stages send it.

Command $D7, a punch. If $24 is 5 or more (a hit in the kick, a punch's lunge or the fall sets it to 10, $714A) the punch is refused and $24 cleared. With the legs in pose $16 (a punch's lunge), $24 is set to 1, and with the torso at position $39 both sequences go back to position $0B for another punch; with the torso at $0D the torso goes to $37 and the legs to $0B; at any other position, on to the arms' test. With the arms in the stance (torso 6, $1C or $1D): from the plain stance (legs 6) the full punch, both sequences from $0A; otherwise the quick punch, the torso alone from $38, while the legs go on. On those paths the hero's punch is marked as taken ($674C: $47 = $80, when the working figure is the hero).

Command $C5, a kick. From the plain stance (legs 6) the kick: legs and torso from position 7 (lift, wind-up, the kick, back). Asked again during the wind-up (legs 1), the wind-up starts again, at most three times ($24). At legs $1B of a step forward, the kick from its wind-up at once. The kick button is marked as taken ($6741).

Command $9B: standing still (legs and torso 7), take the stance (sequence $11 forward); in the stance (legs 6), stand up (sequence $15 backwards). Then $2F, the standing flag, is turned over and the kick button marked as taken.
Command $C2, the bow, only when standing still (legs and torso 7): sequence $16 forward. The punch button is marked as taken.

Command $C6, fall dead: the falling sequence from position $20, unless the figure already lies (legs $0E-$13). The figure is first moved a column back when its column and the dot offset ($50) have the wrong parity for the falling shapes: even for the hero (the working figure is taken to be the hero when its column is $62), odd for anyone else.
If the working figure's column is the hero's ($62), mark the kick request as taken ($46 = $80) so that one press makes one kick.
If the working figure's column is the hero's, mark the punch request as taken ($47 = $80).
Bytes after the command routines that nothing reads, in the pattern of shape data ($AA $D5 ...).
Five entry points: $6780 clears the band behind the opponent ($E5), $6783 draws the working figure, $6786 the opponent's feet mask, $6789 the hero's, $678C clears the band behind the hero ($E3).
JMP: draw the working figure ($6811).
JMP: draw the opponent's feet mask ($6A2E).
Clear the band behind the hero: from column $E3 - 3, as $6797.

Clear the band behind the opponent before he is redrawn: from column $E5 - 6, 11 columns wide (clipped to the screen), rows $72-$98 to black, then rows $99-$A3 to the floor's pattern for the screen ($44) and the stage ($D0): rows of $D5 and $AA in turn, or such rows between black ones, or black, so that the floor comes back where the figure was.

Draw the working figure on the draw page, facing right, or facing left ($2C negative) through $68B3 with the mirrored shape routines. In order: for the torso poses that need it, a mask ($69DC); the legs ($6000 tables; mirrored for the poses $62BE marks); the head's mask ($61D6) and the head or the headgear ($6987); and the torso ($6226 tables). The figure's position is $22 (byte column) with the dot offset $50; rows are offsets from 114. Facing left with $4D not 0 or 5, the stage's own routine at $BC00 draws it instead.
The same for a figure facing left: each offset is taken away from the position and the shapes are drawn mirrored ($190C, $1906).
Add 114 to a shape's row offset and put it in $06.
Set up a feet mask for legs pose X: AND mode ($0F = $FF), its pointer from $60A8/$60D2, its row from $6126.
Set up the legs shape for pose X: OR mode ($0F = 0), pointer from $6000/$602A, column $23, row from $607E.
Draw the legs facing right: mirrored ($1909) for the poses $62BE marks, else as they are ($1903).
Draw the legs facing left: as they are, right-aligned ($1906), for the poses $62BE marks, else mirrored ($190C).

Pick the head for torso pose $21 by its head type ($61A4: 7 and 8 the second and third drawings, the rest the first). Out of the cutscenes ($36 zero) a figure facing right is the hero and wears his own head ($61CA/$61CD); anyone else's is moved up 2 rows and a column back and is the headgear of the opponent type in $3E ($6A6C).
Pick the head's mask for torso pose $21 ($61D6/$61D9, only for the first drawing), first moving the dot position forward by the head type's dots ($6AC5).

For the torso poses 6 and $14-$1D (the stance's arms, the punches and the guards) set up a mask, $9A2A, at the torso's column plus one in the direction faced; for 7, $27 and $0A-$0D (standing and bowing) a smaller one, $9A18, at the torso's column. Returns X = $64 when it set one up, and the caller draws it.
Set up the stance's foot mask, $9A2A, at row $0F + 114, AND mode.
Set up the standing foot mask, $9A18, at row $16 + 114.
Draw the opponent's feet mask (from his record, $70 and $72), mirrored, since opponents face left.
Draw the hero's feet mask (from $60 and $62).
Pick the headgear of opponent type $3E (0-6) for head drawing Y: type 0 and 6 are the engine's ($8ECB..., $8F2B...), types 1-5 the stage's own at $BE00-$BFC3.
Move the dot position ($10, with $23 as the column) forward by A dots, in the direction the figure faces ($2C).
Headgear type 5: high bytes ($BF).
Headgear type 5: low bytes ($BF80, $BFA0, $BFC3).
Headgear type 6, the engine's own: high bytes ($8F).
Headgear type 6: low bytes ($8F2B, $8F4B, $8F6E).
Ten bytes after the headgear tables that nothing reads ($AA $80 $D5 ...).

The opponents' brain: choose a command for the opponent, who is the working figure, and carry it out ($6540). If the hero lies dead (legs $13), a guard (type 0, $4D) in the stance stands up, and any other opponent does nothing. Standing and coming on ($30 set), he walks forward until he is in place, by his column, the hero's ($62), $4B and $4C, and the scroll ($52), then takes the stance; in stages 3 and 4 the brain leaves the walk to the stage. Standing otherwise, at column $27 or less, he takes the stance when the hero is in his stance or within 13 columns ($33), and bows when the hero's legs reach position $1A of their sequences, in the bow. In the stance, while the hero lives: a standing hero is kicked within 8 columns and walked towards further off; a hero in his stance more than 11 columns off is walked towards; nearer, random numbers ($6C95) against the stage's tables, indexed by the distance counted as 7-11 ($BFE1, $BFE6 and $BFEB, with $BFF2 at $6C2F), and the stage's chances in $D7-$D9 choose a kick, a punch, a step forward or nothing. No path steps back.
No command: clear the stick ($29, $2A) and carry out command 0.
A kick at a random height, if the random number is below $D7.

No blow: when the legs' sequence is at position 3, a step forward or a halt, at random against $BFF2 indexed by X; otherwise nothing at all ($6B80). Come from the brain's tables, X is the distance, 7-11, and the read is $BFF9-$BFFD: in every stage $80, the stage's entry jump at $BFFA and its number. After a punch not taken ($6C11, $6C15) X is the opponent's type ($4D, from $6C71); after a kick refused at a standing hero ($6B95), whatever X held when the brain was called.
Seven bytes nothing reaches: LDA #$FF, STA $29, JMP $6540, which would be a step back.
Step forward ($29 = 1), unless the opponent has reached the stage's limit for the first screen ($6C6C by $D0) when $44 is 0.
For each stage ($D0), the column an opponent stops at on the first screen.
A random height for a blow into $2A: $FF (up) below $55, 0 (middle) below $AA, 1 (down) above. Opponent type 1 aims only up or middle, against $80.
The random numbers: $48 = $48 * 17 + $A1, in A.
An earlier copy of the random number routine and zeros to the end of the page; nothing runs it.

Two entry points: $6D00 reads the joystick's position into $29 and $2A, $6D03 its buttons into $46 and $47. The stages call $6D03 several times in each frame, between drawing steps, so that a short press is not missed.
A third JMP to $6D6A that nothing calls.

Read the joystick into $29 (across) and $2A (up and down), each -1, 0 or 1. Touching $C070 starts both paddle timers; the loop counts in $29 and $2A until each timer ($C064, $C065) runs out, or a count reaches 128, the NOP evening out the two paths. Each count becomes -1 below 5, 1 from 45, else 0 ($6DA4). Then CONTROL-E's flag ($C0) swaps the axes, $29 is made relative to the way the figure faces ($2C), so that 1 is forward, with CONTROL-X's flag ($C1) turning it round, and CONTROL-Y's ($C2) turns $2A over.
The other path's timing: a NOP and a branch, as long as the INC.

Read the joystick's buttons, unless the keyboard is chosen ($C4). Each of $46 (kick) and $47 (punch) goes to $FF when its button is pressed, back to 0 when it is let go, and is left alone while it reads $FF (a press not yet taken) or $80 (taken, the button still held: $6741, $674C). Button 0 ($C061) kicks and button 1 ($C062) punches, the other way round when CONTROL-B's flag ($C3) is set.
A paddle count into a direction: below 5 is $FF, below 45 is 0, else 1.
An earlier copy of the input routine below, cut off at $6E00; nothing runs it.

Choose the hero's command, the hero being the working figure, and carry it out ($6540). With the keyboard chosen ($C4) at $6E69. With the joystick: standing, the stick held up keeps him standing (with a new press of button 1, a bow), and letting it go takes the stance. In the stance, a new press of either button kicks or punches at the stick's height; held up, the stick stands him up only when no opponent of type 0 or 1 ($4D) is within 15 columns, the opponent is not type 5 and no hawk is close ($98 set, $91 below $27, $94 negative). Near an opponent, up only aims the next blow high.
Standing, joystick: up and a new press of button 1 ($47) is a bow; up alone, nothing more than the run by the stick; not up, the stance.

The keyboard: first the special keys ($7603), then the key in $C000, lower case taken as capitals. SPACE takes the stance or stands up; LEFT and RIGHT arrows set $29, which stays set while standing (RIGHT runs, LEFT stops the run) and lasts one frame in the stance (one step). In the stance (at $6EAF) Q, A and Z punch high, middle and low, and W, S and X kick high, middle and low; standing (at $6F04), B bows. A punch or kick is kept in $47 or $46 as $FF and sent again each frame until the command takes it, and while one is waiting the next key is thrown away. The key's strobe is cleared at $6EA9.
Clear the key and carry out the command.
In the stance: no movement unless an arrow key set it this frame; a waiting punch goes first, then Q, A, Z, then a waiting kick, then W, S, X ($6EDA), then $6F28.
Standing: a waiting bow ($47 = $FF) is sent again; a waiting stance ($46 = $FF, set by SPACE) too; B asks for the bow.
No key that counts: a waiting kick, else a waiting punch, else command 0.
An earlier copy of the arrows' code (now at $0B12-$0C20 in the low pages: drawing the arrows, taking one off, giving them back), and the code after it; nothing runs it.

The fighters' records: $7000 sets up the hero's, $7003 the opponent's; $7006 saves the working figure ($20-$2F) as the opponent ($70-$7F), $7009 loads him into it; $700C saves it as the hero ($60-$6F), $700F loads the hero; $7012 measures the fight for the pose in A; $7018 and $701B keep $4C and $4B; $701E applies the frame's hits.
JMP: set up the opponent's record ($7048).
JMP: save the working figure as the opponent ($7071).
JMP: load the opponent into the working figure ($707D).
A JMP to $70AC, the distance alone; nothing calls it.
JMP: keep $4C, the hero's side of the screen ($70F0).
Set up the hero's record: standing (legs and torso 7, $6F = $FF) at column $0B, facing right ($6C = 1), the sequences stopped, the stick centred, the height up ($6A = $FF).
Set up the opponent's record: standing at column $30, facing left ($7C = $FF), the sequences stopped; $4B cleared.
Copy the working figure ($20-$2F) to the opponent's record ($70-$7F).
Copy the opponent's record into the working figure, then measure the fight against the hero's legs pose ($60).
Copy the working figure to the hero's record ($60-$6F).
Copy the hero's record into the working figure, then measure the fight against the opponent's legs pose ($70).

For the other fighter's legs pose in A, put his pose class ($70C6) in $32 and the distance between the two, the opponent's column less the hero's ($72 - $62), in $33; $FF in $33 while $4B and $4C differ and the scroll ($52) is 0-$30, when the two are not on the same screen.

For each of the 42 legs poses, its class for the hit test ($7366): poses 0-7 (the kick's, the stance and standing) their own classes 0-7; poses 8-$16 (rising into the stance, the bow, the fall, the punch's lunge) class 6 or 7; poses $17-$29 (the steps and the run) classes 8-$19.
Keep $4C, the side the hero is on during a scroll: his column on the screen, $30 - $52 + $62, at 0-4 sets it to 1, at -5 to -1 sets it to 0, elsewhere leaves it.
The same for the opponent and $4B, by $30 - $52 + $72.
A blow on a figure standing, running or bowing: if it is the hero (his column is the working figure's), he dies of it ($7131); an opponent does not.
The hero dies: no arrows left ($B6) and not alive ($5D). For a collision (Y = 4) the struck sound too ($42), $40 one less and $7A cleared. Then the fall ($7145).
